messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a small but consistent output drift after swapping the ROPE kernel variant in the canary cluster. Not huge, but it trips a couple eval prompts at long sequence lengths (>8k).

oliver: How tiny are we talking? abs-diff per token or log-prob shift?

maria: Mostly per-token float diff. Max abs diff ~1e-3 on some attention logits, but concentrated in late tokens where accumulators blow up. Causes rerank changes in a handful of prompts.

jin: Thanks — that pattern smells like precision accumulation + different reduction order between old/new kernel paths. Are we hitting bf16 paths?

maria: Canary nodes are on mixed path: kernel picks bfloat16-friendly matmul but we left accumulators in fp32. New impl uses a fused accumulate that seems to reorder ops.

sophie: Does this reproduce locally with the unit test harness? Could add a deterministic seed and long-sequence fuzz run.

maria: I ran a micro-repro: small Python harness with rng seed, a 12B model slice, seq_len=16384 — reproduces deterministically.

oliver: Let's add lightweight sanity asserts in the runtime kernel selector: when choosing the new ROPE path, run a cheap shadow check that computes max_abs_diff of attention logits vs reference kernel for first N tokens (N=64). If > threshold (e.g. 1e-2) log and failover.

jin: Agreed. Also add an accumulative histogram metric: attention_logit_diff_p95/p99 by seq_bucket. That will surface long-seq issues without full captures.

maria: Proposed quick guard code snippet for selector (pseudocode):
```
if (selector == ROPE_FUSED) {
  ref = run_kernel(ROPE_REF, sample_heads)
  cand = run_kernel(ROPE_FUSED, sample_heads)
  if (max_abs(ref-cand) > EPSILON) {
    emit_metric("posenc.diff.fail", max_abs)
    fallback_to(ROPE_REF)
  }
}
```

oliver: Nice. For EPSILON we should choose per-dtype and per-seqlen bucket. Suggest baseline_map = {fp32:1e-5, bf16:1e-3}. And multiply by sqrt(seq_len/512) as heuristic.

sophie: Operationally, prefer rollout in shadow-mode for 48h with metric alert if >0.1% of requests exceed threshold. Shadow-mode means run fused kernel but do not serve its outputs; only collect diffs.

jin: Also add unit tests: 1) deterministic long-seq seeded fuzz up to 65k, 2) head-wise reduction order permutations, 3) bfloat16 quantized path vs fp32 reference. Should be fast—run in CI nightly.

maria: I'll open a small RFC PR that: adds selector shadow check, telemetry histograms, config knobs (epsilon_map, shadow=true), and a new fuzz test harness. Will link the PR here.

runtime-ci-bot: Created job 987654: ci/posenc-fuzz-nightly for branch posenc-sanity-checks.

oliver: One more edge: we saw some NaN/Inf cases in older threads. Add a tiny clamp on exponentials and a sentinel that forces fallback if any NaN/Inf seen in attention kernel.

jin: Good call. For clamping, use stable logsumexp safety: if any logit > 1e6 or isNaN then fallback. Also capture RNG seed for repro.

sophie: If we add shadow checks, ensure the selector won't cause 2x latency on tail if both kernels compute on hot path. Run only on 1% sampling at high qps, or sample by token_bucket.

maria: Plan: implement shadow-mode + histogram + NaN/Inf guard this week. Run 1% sampled shadow canary for 72h. If diffs exceed 0.5% of sampled requests or p99 diff > 1e-2, auto-roll back new kernel globally.

oliver: I'll add the per-dtype epsilon map and the seq_len scaling logic. Also add a small benchmark to measure shadow overhead and memory bump.

jin: I'll owner the fuzz harness and the seeded repro artifacts. Will post a repro tarball in the PR.

sophie: I'll wire alerts in Datadog: posenc.diff.fail.rate, posenc.nan.count, posenc.shadow.latency.p95. Thresholds in PR.

maria: Thanks. If anyone finds other examples, drop them in the PR thread. Quick note: keep changes confined to kernel-selector, no global API surface changes — want fast rollback. :thumbsup:

runtime-ci-bot: Job 987654 passed initial compile checks. Tests queued: posenc-fuzz-nightly, posenc-shadow-smoke.
